series.name: The Professor's Bet
series.tagline: Twelve students. Twelve pitches. One quiet rebel.
series.concept: Last semester at IIM Bangalore. Prof. Anand Iyer (58, ex-VC, fund blew up in 2019) teaches Strategy. On Day 1 he writes 'Competition is for losers' on the board and bets ₹50 lakh of his own money that none of his 12 students will build a monopoly. Each Tuesday a student pitches; he uses one Thiel framework from Zero to One to dismantle it. In the back row, Meera Nair from Kollam doesn't speak — she is quietly building Bahi, a voice-first AI for India's small traders. In Episode 11 she finally pitches. Every framework checks out. In Episode 12 the professor writes a cheque.

episodes.title: The Bet

slides.text:
Tuesday, 9 AM. Strategy elective. IIM Bangalore.

The class doesn't know yet — this is the professor's last term.

He walks in. No preamble.

He picks up a piece of chalk and writes one sentence.

Competition is for losers.

— Peter Thiel

By the end of this term, none of you will have built a monopoly.

I will personally fund anyone who proves me wrong.

₹50 lakh. My money. Not the institute's.

The class laughs.

He doesn't smile.

The laugh stops.

Front row: Sir, what counts as a monopoly?

Professor: When you're so good at one thing, competition can't touch you.

Google. Not Bing. Not Yahoo. Google.

Back row.

Meera Nair. 24. Kollam. Notebook open.

She writes one word, then underlines it.

Bahi.

Next Tuesday.

Rohan pitches. Healthy food delivery.

The professor reaches for his marker.

episodes.synopsis: Day 1 of the Strategy elective. Prof. Anand Iyer enters with no preamble. Writes 'Competition is for losers' on the board. Turns. Bets ₹50 lakh of his own money that nobody in this room will build a monopoly by the end of the term. The class laughs. The laugh stops. Cut to the back row — Meera Nair, notebook open, writing one word and underlining it: Bahi.
episodes.caption:
the bet is real. ₹50 lakh of his own money.

what would you build if you had to prove you weren't a loser?

episodes.title: Competition is for Losers
episodes.synopsis: Rohan pitches a healthy food delivery startup — 'Swiggy for clean eating, we focus on quality.' The professor draws Swiggy, Zomato, EatFit, FreshMenu, and three others on the board, asks which one died last quarter, and asks Rohan why he wants to be the next to die. Better quality is not a moat. It is a slogan.

episodes.title: Last Mover Advantage
episodes.synopsis: Aarti pitches an AI productivity OS — 'we're first to market.' The professor lists six 'first AI productivity tools' that have already shut down. Being first means you fund everyone else's research. The last mover takes the market and holds it. Google was not first. Facebook was not first. Be the last one standing.

episodes.title: 1 to N vs 0 to 1
episodes.synopsis: Vivek pitches 'Uber for laundry, AI-optimised pickup.' The professor draws two arrows on the board — horizontal for 1-to-n, vertical for 0-to-1. Copying a model with AI sprinkled on top is not innovation. It is globalisation. Capitalism is horizontal. Technology is vertical. Vivek is doing horizontal in a market with negative unit economics.

episodes.title: The Four Monopoly Powers
episodes.synopsis: Sanjana pitches a D2C skincare brand — 'clean ingredients, Mama Earth for Gen Z.' The professor draws a 2x2: proprietary tech, network effects, economies of scale, branding. He hands her the marker. She fills only the branding box. The other three stay empty. You need all four. Most D2C brands have only the fourth.

episodes.title: The Power Law
episodes.synopsis: Karthik pitches 'a neobank for Bharat — we aim to be a top 5 player.' The professor draws a long-tail curve on the board. Marks #1. Marks the abyss after. Returns are not normally distributed. The #1 takes more than #2 through #10 combined. There is no top 5. There is #1, and there is dead.

episodes.title: The Secret
episodes.synopsis: Open class day. The professor goes around the room with one question — what important truth do very few people agree with you on? Most students answer with opinions. Some with hot takes. None with a real secret. The professor rejects every answer. In the back row, Meera doesn't raise her hand. She writes one sentence in her notebook and closes it: Indian SMBs don't want software. They want a bahi-khata that listens.

episodes.title: Sales is the Product
episodes.synopsis: Akshay, all engineer, no sleep, pitches an AI ops tool — 'engineers will love it, the product will sell itself.' The professor asks him to name his first ten customers by name. He names two. No product sells itself. Distribution is half the company. You don't sell only to customers — you sell to investors, employees, yourself every morning. Akshay doesn't have a go-to-market. He has a deck.

episodes.title: Foundations
episodes.synopsis: Tanvi and Dev pitch a marketplace for short-form video editors. They look like cofounders. The professor asks how they met — in this class. Who is CEO? — we haven't decided. Equity split? — 50-50. He turns to the board and writes one word: Doomed. A startup messed up at its foundation cannot be fixed. Cofounders should know each other longer than they have known the startup.

episodes.title: Man and Machine
episodes.synopsis: Riya pitches AI agents that replace call centre workers — 'unit economics destroy the incumbents.' The professor draws two circles: HUMAN and MACHINE. Where is the overlap? What does the human in the loop add that the machine cannot? Riya doesn't answer. Computers complement humans. They don't replace them. The big companies of the next 30 years will be man-and-machine, not machine-versus-man.

episodes.title: The Seven Questions
episodes.synopsis: Meera finally pitches. Bahi — voice-first AI on WhatsApp for India's small traders, in their own language. The professor reaches for his marker and asks Thiel's seven questions. Engineering: vernacular voice models trained on trader speech. Timing: WhatsApp Business is finally ubiquitous and GST 2.0 forces monthly filings. Monopoly: 50,000 traders in one tier-2 cluster first. People: she grew up in a trader family. Distribution: trade associations, temple groups. Durability: voice-data moat compounds. Secret: Indian SMBs don't want software, they want a bahi-khata that listens. He puts the marker down. He doesn't reach for it again.

episodes.title: The Professor Pays
episodes.synopsis: Last Tuesday of the term. The professor enters with an envelope. No marker. No preamble. He places the envelope on Meera's desk. He turns to the class. 'I bet against you. I lost. The lesson isn't that she won. The lesson is that she was the only one in this room who wasn't competing. She was building.' India runs on indefinite optimism — we'll figure it out. Founders who win run on definite optimism — this is the plan, here is the secret nobody else has seen. Final sentence on the board: Don't try to be the next Google. The next Google won't do anything Google does. Find your own zero to one.
